set.body:
ModelFormula is a real ADT but its own fields keep column and term references as bare String:

  final case class ModelFormula(onset: String, terms: Vector[TermCall])
  ArgValue.Ident(value: String)                              // a column reference
  HrfCall(id: Option[String], prefix: Option[String], ...)   // term identifiers

ArgValue.Ident("cond") is where a column name stays untyped from parse all the way to the runtime lookup — and that is precisely the path that yields BuildFailed instead of MissingColumn. The error-fidelity defect (bd-01KYYK1XFSXA49DQDRVDCT77KJ) is the visible symptom of this one rather than a separate problem.

Change:
  ModelFormula(onset: ColumnId, ...)
  ArgValue.Ident(value: ColumnId)
  HrfCall(id: Option[TermId], prefix: Option[TermId], ...)

FormulaParser becomes the boundary that lifts text into ids; the build path then carries a ColumnId into the total accessor, which returns MissingColumn / InvalidColumnType structurally.

NOT in scope: basis: Option[String] and basisClass: String. They key the user-extensible BasisRegistry, so an open set is correct.

Sequencing: must come AFTER the ColumnId round-trip fix (bd-01KYYK1VED50YQP6FFSHX099HW). Typing these fields first would push the silent-rename bug into the formula path, where TermId("a.b") rewrites a user's term name to a_b.

Blast radius measured: the formula AST has exactly one downstream main consumer outside its own package — fmri-workflow/AnalysisSpec.scala, 4 sites.

Context: docs/plans/design-hardening.md section 3.4 and phase 3.
set.title: Type the formula AST's column and term references
